accuracy.evidence: Checked against the EEF guidance report Metacognition and Self-Regulated Learning (2018/2021), which frames learning as plan, monitor and evaluate, and against Kolb's experiential learning cycle (concrete experience, reflective observation, abstract conceptualisation, active experimentation) and Gibbs' reflective cycle. Feed forward is attributed correctly to Hattie and Timperley's three questions (Where am I going? How am I going? Where to next?). The lesson does not overclaim: it presents reflecting as one evaluate stage that feeds the next plan, and warns that a high score can come from luck.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented ideas that a good mark means nothing to learn (prediction No, 8 is a good score; tag score), that reflection is a general feeling (Fractions are hard. Try harder.; tag vague), that failure is someone else's fault (The glue was rubbish; tag blame), that only mistakes matter (tag onlybad, and the lab shows skipping the bar model lowers session 2), that repeating the same method will change the result (tag same) and that reflecting later is as good as soon after (tag late).

lab_distinct.evidence: flaglookback is a session-replay model: learners tag six moments of one homework timeline, tune three slots of a reflection until a usefulness meter fills, place the four cycle stages on a ring, choose two changes and re-run session 2 for a new score, and drag four pupils onto a score against next-step grid. flagreflect and the other Learning to Learn labs have no timeline replay or re-run mechanic, and the 30 percent shingle gate passed against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Cause comes before the words: tagging shows two confusing moments behind an 8/10, the meter only fills when every slot names an exact strategy or step, session 2 reaches 10/10 only when both lost-mark moments are fixed and drops when the bar model is skipped, and the grid places Kit (low score, no next step) apart from Leo (high score, knows what to do next). Each done message states the idea after the evidence is on screen.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options the lab then tests: No, 8 is a good score (the replay finds two fixable moments), Fractions are hard. Try harder. (the meter stays at 0 of 3 for vague lines) and Do it exactly the same or Skip the bar model to save time (session 2 stays at 8 or falls). A.reveal repeats the learner's own pick next to the right answer.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating questions (spelling test, fallen science model, timing, what to include, times tables) with every wrong answer tagged to its own message: score (the score tells you how it went, not why), vague (name the exact step, like the bar model or the double s), blame, same, late and onlybad (in the lab, skipping the bar model made things worse). Option order rotates so the useful reflection is not always first.

readability.evidence: Learner audience for age 9 to 10: kid paragraphs are short, concrete sentences built around one example (I could not find a common denominator) and pass the learner kid limit; the adult text was rewritten into short sentences that still use the exact terms metacognition, plan-monitor-evaluate, strategy, evaluation and feed forward, and now passes the learner adult limit. Lab slot labels are three or four words (What helped, What was confusing, Next time I will).

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate passed and overlap with the existing reflection, mistakes and growth lessons is under 12 percent. Each kid paragraph adds one idea (score versus process, the three questions with a specific-versus-vague pair, keeping what worked, the loop and timing); adult paragraphs give the framework links, key words, six named mistakes with the lucky-score caution, and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark after every Show me: the six-moment timeline fits with emoji above and tags below, the Helped and Confusing buttons are full half-width tap targets, the three reflection slots wrap to two lines without clipping, the cycle labels sit clear of the ring and the moving dot is now drawn behind them, the four change cards are full width, and the grid pupils are 44 px circles. Every canvas action has a full-width button twin.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed: axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone 13, no console or page errors, every Show me task completed and the challenge appeared. Tagging, slot changes, change picks and grid placement all work by buttons as well as tap or drag, the aria-label speaks each result (Moment 6: it helped. Checking caught a slip.) and tags use words and emoji, not colour alone.
